edges.effect_quant: Pooled meta-analytic evidence suggest the direction is more reliable than any single pooled magnitude.
edges.mechanism: Coffee delivers caffeine plus polyphenols that can pull risk in opposite directions: caffeine acutely raises blood pressure and sleep arousal, while habitual intake is linked with better insulin sensitivity and lower liver fat. The net effect on Sleep quality therefore tends to depend on dose, tolerance, and whether the endpoint is metabolic benefit or overstimulation.
edges.summary: Heavy coffee intake appears tied to worse sleep quality in general adult mainly through pooled meta-analytic evidence. The likely magnitude is modest, which is why the edge is framed conservatively rather than as a headline-level breakthrough.
edges.caveats: Dose and timing matter, and smoking status historically confounded some coffee cohorts. These edges are about habitual intake patterns, not about one caffeinated serving in isolation.
